new_statements.rule_in_words: Only snippets: Klingenheben speaks of a 'Pänultima-Akzent' (penultimate accent) that lengthens an epenthetic vowel, and of the 'Starkton' (strong stress) falling on the penultimate syllable of reube 'women'. No general statement of the stress rule was seen; the deciding sentence is not in the snippets.
new_statements.identity_note: Faidherbe 1882 explicitly describes 'l'idiome des Toucouleurs du Fouta sénégalais' (p. 13), i.e. Senegalese Pulaar, despite the MPI record's ISO tag fub. Bickoe 2000 describes fulfuldé fuunaaŋgere, 'Ful of the East', the variety of the Diamaré department around Maroua, Extrême-Nord Cameroon, following Noye's Diamaré dictionary (introduction; text-file lines 316-326); the MPI record tags it fuv (Nigerian Fulfulde) while Glottolog files it under adam1253, and Bickoe's Arnott quotation concerns the Gombe (Nigeria) dialect. Klingenheben 1927 is a comparative phonology across Ful dialects (Adamaua, Masina, Kano, Futa Damga, Bagirmi) built on Westermann's Handbuch dialect; the snippets do not say which dialect the penultimate-accent remarks concern.

new_statements.translation: p. 63: "we found that tone has no distinctive value in Fulfulde Fuunaangere [...] Fulfulde Fuunaangere is not a tone language. It simply has a stress accent (accent tonique) which, moreover, is nonetheless perceptible in every word." p. 64: "1) Verbs and adjectives: these are generally accented on the first syllable of their root. [...] 2) Two-syllable nouns: these too are accented on the first syllable. [...] 3) Nouns of more than two syllables: these are generally accented on the second-to-last syllable or on the penultimate syllable. Examples: rawàandu 'dog', laamíido 'sultan', tùmmude 'calabash', ùnordu 'mortar'"

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Adamawa Fulani carries no rule; this is the only opened work actually on an Adamawa-area variety (Fulfulde Fuunaangere of Maroua / Diamaré, Extrême-Nord Cameroon) and it supplies: no tone, non-contrastive stress, root-initial for verbs/adjectives, initial for disyllabic nouns, antepenult-or-penult for longer nouns. It is not a fixed: penultimate syllable statement, so it does not simply agree with Faidherbe's Senegal statement or Klingenheben's 'Pänultima-Akzent' snippet.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No lexical tone; a non-contrastive stress accent present in every word. Placement by word class: verbs and adjectives on the first syllable of the root; disyllabic nouns on the first syllable; longer nouns 'on the avant-dernière or the pénultième syllable' (the two French terms both mean penult, but his own examples split: rawàandu, laamíido penult with a long vowel; tùmmude, ùnordu initial = antepenult). Adverbs of intensity carry a very marked accent, usually on a higher pitch. Bickoe attributes the placements to Noye, Taylor, Klingenheben, Arnott and Stennes, and quotes Arnott 1970:62 'Fula is an intonational rather than a tonal language'. Possible long-vowel-penult sensitivity is my inference from the examples, not his statement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned; adverbs intensifying adjectives/verbs get 'un accent très marqué, et ordinairement sur un ton plus élevé' (p. 64)
new_statements.exceptions: 'généralement' for all three placement rules; rule 3 is internally garbled (avant-dernière = pénultième) and its examples show both initial/antepenult and penult
new_statements.identity_note: Faidherbe 1882 explicitly describes 'l'idiome des Toucouleurs du Fouta sénégalais' (p. 13), i.e. Senegalese Pulaar, despite the MPI record's ISO tag fub. Bickoe 2000 describes fulfuldé fuunaaŋgere, 'Ful of the East', the variety of the Diamaré department around Maroua, Extrême-Nord Cameroon, following Noye's Diamaré dictionary (introduction; text-file lines 316-326); the MPI record tags it fuv (Nigerian Fulfulde) while Glottolog files it under adam1253, and Bickoe's Arnott quotation concerns the Gombe (Nigeria) dialect. Klingenheben 1927 is a comparative phonology across Ful dialects (Adamaua, Masina, Kano, Futa Damga, Bagirmi) built on Westermann's Handbuch dialect; the snippets do not say which dialect the penultimate-accent remarks concern.

readall_conflicts: Faidherbe 1882 (Senegalese Pulaar of Futa Toro, p. 12) says the accent is 'generally on the penultimate syllable', and the Klingenheben 1927 snippets (pp. 22, 58, dialect of Westermann's Handbuch) speak of a 'Pänultima-Akzent' and strong stress on the penult; Bickoe 2000 (Fulfulde Fuunaangere of Maroua/Diamaré, pp. 63-65), the only work on the target variety, says tone is non-distinctive and there is a non-contrastive stress accent placed by word class: first syllable of the root for verbs and adjectives, first syllable of disyllabic nouns, and for longer nouns either the antepenult or the penult (his examples: tùmmude, ùnordu vs rawàandu, laamíido). So the Senegal/general sources give penult, while the Adamawa-area thesis gives an initial-dominant, class-conditioned placement that is penultimate only in some longer nouns (those with a long penult vowel in his examples). Bickoe's rule 3 is also internally garbled ('avant-dernière ou pénultième' are the same syllable in French).

sources.quote: 'The accent is predominantly a stress accent, and, generally speaking, depends on the long vowels.' Disyllables: (1) if the first vowel is long or diphthongal it has the accent (sudu, ndi); (2) if two medial consonants or first vowel short, 'the accent is even' (nagge, puchu); (3) accent on the last syllable in the negative past (o warai) and nogas 'twenty'. Trisyllables: (1) long penult has the accent (lamido, rawandu); (2) short penult -> accent on the first vowel (karehi, derewol, o heniti; all trisyllabic derived verbs). 'In polysyllables the accent is free, but is usually on the penultima

sources.note: The grammar states on the next page (p. 13): "C'est l'idiome des Toucouleurs du Fouta sénégalais que nous allons étudier ici. Il présente quelques petites différences avec le poul pur et des différences plus considérables avec les idiomes pouls plus ou moins corrompus du grand empire poul compris entre le Niger et le lac Tchad." So the work describes Senegalese Pulaar (Futa Toro / Toucouleur), not Adamawa Fulfulde, although the MPI record tags it ISO fub. If read as a pan-Fula statement it would supply a penultimate placement to a catalog entry that has none (refines).
